parsed.basis: Triesenberg is a small alpine municipality in Liechtenstein's Oberland above Vaduz, with no local law separate from the national regime. Same-sex relations are lawful and sexual-orientation discrimination is prohibited, but gender identity has no explicit anti-discrimination protection and there is no local procedure to align Liechtenstein-issued documents with gender, while no law bars access to sex-segregated facilities. The municipality is socially close-knit and predominantly Catholic, with a rural, less anonymous character than the capital and tourism concentrated around Malbun, so a trans visitor is more visible and likely to face staring, curiosity or conservative disapproval. National policing and courts are lawful and generally protective, with no documented criminalisation of gender expression.
